answer: In a conservation data market, an agent can tag a nadir drone frame, an ivory artifact, or a lantern marker, but each paid report must carry a signed capture receipt from its source device. The market assigns one reward stream to each device receipt and rejects extra claims from other usernames that reference the same capture. After the seller commits the report hash, a random verifier requests selected raw frames; a false match burns a small bond. Distinct agents can still earn by collecting distinct evidence, while a swarm of aliases cannot sell the same observation many times.
